items.readable_text:
Content:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

Content:
[MATH: \cos(x+y) = \cos x \cos y - \sin x \sin y]

Content:
Substituting [MATH: y={\color{blue}x}] into the above gives

Content:
[MATH: \cos (x + x)|= \cos x\cos x − \sin x\sin x,]

Content:
which simplifies to

Content:
[MATH: \cos 2x = \cos^2 {x} - \sin^2 {x}.]

Content:
This is called the double-angle formula for cosine.

items.readable_text:
Content:
It's possible to write the double angle formula for cosine in two alternative forms.

Content:
From the Pythagorean identity [MATH: \sin^2{x}+\cos^2{x}=1,] we obtain [MATH: \cos^2{x}=1-\sin^2{x}.]
Substituting this into the double-angle formula for cosine, we get

Content:
[MATH: \cos 2x|= \cos^{2} x − \sin^{2} x; = (1 − \sin^{2} x) − \sin^{2} x; = 1 − 2\sin^{2} x.]

Content:
This gives an alternative form of the double-angle formula for cosine. We'll restate it below:
[MATH: \cos{2x} =1 - 2\sin^2{x}]

Content:
Similarly, from the same Pythagorean identity, we obtain that [MATH: \sin^2{x}=1-\cos^2{x}.] Substituting into the double-angle formula for cosine, we get

Content:
[MATH: \cos 2x|= \cos^{2} x − \sin^{2} x; = \cos^{2} x − (1 − \cos^{2} x); = 2\cos^{2} x − 1.]

Content:
This is another alternative form of the double-angle formula for cosine:
[MATH: \cos{2x} =2\cos^2{x}-1]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

Content:
[MATH: \cos(x+y) = \cos x \cos y - \sin x \sin y]

Content:
Substituting [MATH: y={\color{blue}x}] into the above gives

Content:
[MATH: \cos (x + x)|= \cos x\cos x − \sin x\sin x,]

Content:
which simplifies to

Content:
[MATH: \cos 2x = \cos^2 {x} - \sin^2 {x}.]

Content:
This is called the double-angle formula for cosine.

---

Item 2 — Example: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Expressions

Example Prompt:
Express [MATH: \cos^2{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)} - \sin^2{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)}] as a single trigonometric ratio.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

[MATH: \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x = \cos 2x]

Substituting [MATH: x={\dfrac{\pi}{24}}] into the above, we get

[MATH: \cos^{2} ((π)/(24)) − \sin^{2} ((π)/(24))|= \cos (2 ⋅ (π)/(24)); = \cos ((π)/(12)).]

Item 5 — Tutorial: Alternative Forms of the Double-Angle Formula for Cosine

Content:
It's possible to write the double angle formula for cosine in two alternative forms.

Content:
From the Pythagorean identity [MATH: \sin^2{x}+\cos^2{x}=1,] we obtain [MATH: \cos^2{x}=1-\sin^2{x}.]
Substituting this into the double-angle formula for cosine, we get

Content:
[MATH: \cos 2x|= \cos^{2} x − \sin^{2} x; = (1 − \sin^{2} x) − \sin^{2} x; = 1 − 2\sin^{2} x.]

Content:
This gives an alternative form of the double-angle formula for cosine. We'll restate it below:
[MATH: \cos{2x} =1 - 2\sin^2{x}]

Content:
Similarly, from the same Pythagorean identity, we obtain that [MATH: \sin^2{x}=1-\cos^2{x}.] Substituting into the double-angle formula for cosine, we get

Content:
[MATH: \cos 2x|= \cos^{2} x − \sin^{2} x; = \cos^{2} x − (1 − \cos^{2} x); = 2\cos^{2} x − 1.]

Content:
This is another alternative form of the double-angle formula for cosine:
[MATH: \cos{2x} =2\cos^2{x}-1]

Explanation:

[MATH: 2 \cos^2 x - 1 = \cos 2x]

Substituting [MATH: x={\dfrac{\pi}{3}}] into the above, we get

[MATH: 2\cos^{2} ((π)/(3)) − 1|= \cos (2 ⋅ (π)/(3)); = \cos ((2π)/(3)).]
